etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English equaten, from Latin aequātus, perfect passive participle of aequō, see -ate (verb-forming suffix).

definitions.definition: (transitive) To consider equal or equivalent (to or with).

quote.citation: 1960 February, “Talking of Trains”, in Trains Illustrated, page 67:
quote.text: Mr. Hoyle, who does not believe many multiple-unit diesel services on secondary routes will resist for ever the road transport challenge, would forgo passenger traffic altogether on a little-used route in order to improve the quality of the freight working and reduce its costs by equating the average speed of all trains on the line concerned.

definitions.definition: (programming) A statement in assembly language that defines a symbol having a particular value.

quote.citation: 2005, Arnold S. Berger, Hardware and Computer Organization, page 220:
quote.text: The first section of the program includes the system equates.

quote.citation: 2009, Saifullah Khalid, Neetu Agrawal, Microprocessor System, page 256:
quote.text: The following equates define the stats byte  […]

quote.citation: 2012, J. S. Anderson, Microprocessor Technology, page 221:
quote.text: You can learn much about user routines, labels, displacements, equates (EQU) and so on, by modifying this program and observing the results on the screen.
